title: Tunable Polycaprolactone-Gelatin Methacryloyl Composites for Fused Deposition Modeling Musculoskeletal Scaffold Fabrication.
abstract: The global musculoskeletal burden continues to outpace standard of care transplantation efforts and existing tissue engineering solutions, necessitating further development of scalable biomaterials. In this study, we introduce a novel synthesis of polycaprolactone-gelatin methacryloyl (PCL-GelMA) composite filament, compatible with standard fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printers, for scalable and customizable scaffold fabrication. By incorporating 15% and 30% (w/w) GelMA into a PCL matrix, we achieved tunable modulation of surface roughness, hydrophilicity, and degradation kinetics. Mechanical testing revealed nonlinear dependencies between GelMA content and tensile properties, suggesting that variation in GelMA particle size and distribution leads to a concentration-dependent trade-off between stiffness and structural integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) cultured on printed scaffolds maintained viability and proliferative capacity. By mitigating solvent toxicity through upstream processing, physically integrating constituents into a unified bulk matrix, and leveraging the accessibility of FDM printing, this material platform enables scalable translation and further biomaterial exploration.
journal: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part A

title: Laser-programmed anisotropic hierarchical host bone interfaces for mechanotransduction-guided osseointegration.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional mechanical osteotomy often induces thermal and mechanical damage, which compromises the biological quality of the host bone interface and impairs subsequent osseointegration. This study aimed to develop a 9.3 μm CO2 laser-based osteotomy strategy that integrates precise bone cutting with in situ regenerative interface engineering.
METHODS: A 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation.
RESULTS: The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration.
THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS ARTICLE: 9.3 μm CO2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. These findings provide a regenerative osteotomy strategy for improving the biological quality of surgically created bone interfaces, which holds translational potential for orthopedic implant surgery, fracture reconstruction, and the repair of bone defects in clinical practice.

title: Biomaterial-assisted culture of mesenchymal stem cells for enhanced extracellular vesicle production and cartilage regeneration: a systematic review.
abstract: Articular cartilage has limited self-repair capacity, prompting interest in cell-free therapies such as extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). This systematic review assessed whether MSCs cultured with biomaterials produce more EVs, and EVs with greater chondrogenic or cartilage-regenerative efficacy, than MSCs in conventional culture. The publications were searched on PubMed, Scopus, and EBSCO (2016-2026), and the synthesis of the evidence was done narratively, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From 576 unique records, we included 14 preclinical studies: 12 used biomaterials in a three-dimensional format, and two cultured MSCs on decellularized extracellular matrix. Eleven compared biomaterial-culture EVs head-to-head with conventional-culture EVs for chondrogenic or cartilage-repair outcomes. EV yield was higher with the biomaterial in all ten studies that compared it (about 1.2- to 7.5-fold per cell or per unit of protein). In all 11 comparisons, biomaterial-culture EVs matched or exceeded conventional-culture EVs in chondrocyte proliferation, chondrogenic marker expression, matrix deposition, or in vivo cartilage repair. Cargo-target mechanisms were functionally validated in six studies, although in one the microRNA had been enriched by transfection rather than by the culture platform. Certainty of evidence was low for yield and very low for chondrogenic, cartilage-repair, and anti-inflammatory outcomes. Risk of bias was probably low in seven studies and probably high in seven. The comparator arms often differed in more than the biomaterial, and EV characterization was frequently incomplete. In conclusion, biomaterial-assisted culture is a promising but not yet standardized route to more chondrogenic MSC-derived EVs and requires further study.

title: Restoring the repair-fibrosis balance via a localized extracellular vesicle-pirfenidone dual-delivery biomaterial platform promotes ureteral repair after thermal injury.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ureteral thermal injury can lead to ureteral stricture through persistent oxidative stress, inflammation, impaired vascular repair, and excessive fibrosis. Current treatment strategies primarily aim to restore urinary drainage or address established structural obstruction, whereas approaches that simultaneously modulate tissue repair and postinjury fibrotic remodeling remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a localized dual-delivery biomaterial platform that simultaneously promotes tissue repair and suppresses excessive fibrosis after ureteral thermal injury.
METHODS: A localized EG_PFM platform was fabricated by combining a mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicle (MSC-EV)-loaded chitosan/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (EG) with a pirfenidone (PF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanofibrous membrane (PFM). The physicochemical properties and release profiles were characterized. In vitro, the effects of MSC-EVs and PF on urothelial and smooth muscle cell relative cell growth and migration, oxidative stress, angiogenesis, macrophage phenotype, and fibrosis-associated cellular responses were evaluated. A rabbit model of ureteral thermal injury was established to assess ureteral structural repair, hydronephrosis, collagen deposition, oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, and transcriptomic changes.
RESULTS: EG_PFM exhibited favorable biocompatibility, tissue adhesion, and sustained release of MSC-EVs and PF. MSC-EVs increased relative cell growth and enhanced the migration of urothelial and smooth muscle cells, reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species, enhanced endothelial tube formation and were associated with an M2-like macrophage phenotype, whereas PF suppressed α-SMA expression and extracellular matrix accumulation. In rabbits, EG_PFM reduced hydronephrosis and ureteral stricture, decreased collagen deposition, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses, and enhanced vascularization. Transcriptomic analysis identified treatment-associated changes in multiple signaling and metabolic pathways, including calcium signaling, cell adhesion molecules, tyrosine metabolism, and retinol metabolism.
CONCLUSION: Localized codelivery of MSC-EVs and PF promoted reparative responses while limiting fibrotic remodeling, thereby improving structural repair after ureteral thermal injury. EG_PFM represents a promising localized therapeutic strategy for reducing postinjury ureteral stricture.

title: Strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite scaffolds enhance bone regeneration by promoting macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype.
abstract: The development of synthetic bone grafts that integrate osteogenic and immunomodulatory functions represents a critical strategy in regenerative orthopedics. In this study, we fabricated strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite (HA/Mg/Sr) scaffolds derived from natural bovine cancellous bone. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the preservation of a three-dimensional interconnected porous architecture (∼80% porosity, ∼350 μm pore size) with a homogeneous nanoparticulate surface. Doping with Mg and Sr enhanced scaffold degradation, sustained the release of bioactive ions (,,), and significantly increased compressive strength to levels comparable with human cancellous bone.In vitro, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoting adhesion and proliferation of both bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs). While Mg primarily facilitated direct osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, Sr played a dominant role in directing macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, as evidenced by increased CD206 and IL-10 expression alongside reduced CCR7 and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Notably, macrophage-conditioned medium from HA/Mg/Sr cultures substantially enhanced BMSC osteogenesis, highlighting immunomodulation as a central mechanism. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that the HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype and modulated immune responses potentially through the NF-κB signaling pathway, which was validated by Western blot. In a rat femoral condyle defect model, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds-particularly those with 10% Sr content (HA/Mg/Sr2)-demonstrated superior bone regeneration, characterized by bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), trabecular number (Tb.N) and enhanced new bone ingrowth and integration, accompanied by elevated M2 macrophage infiltrationin vivo. Overall, these findings establish that HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promote bone repair not only via direct osteoconduction but, more importantly, through immunomodulation-fostering a pro-healing M2 macrophage microenvironment potentially in an NF-κB-dependent manner, thereby offering a promising dual-functional biomaterial strategy for critical-sized bone defect reconstruction. Collectively, this study underscores the therapeutic relevance of targeting macrophage polarization in bone repair and delineates a mechanistic framework for Sr-based immunomodulatory biomaterial design.

title: Tissue-Specific Regulation of Glucose and Lipid Metabolism by miR-29a in Insulin Resistance and Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: MicroRNA-29a (miR-29a) has emerged as a context-dependent regulator of glucose and lipid metabolism in insulin-sensitive tissues, yet its tissue-specific actions in insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes remain incompletely understood. We synthesized peer-reviewed evidence retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost on the role of miR-29a across skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, liver, and pancreatic β-cells. We first define the nomenclature and genomic organization of the miR-29 family, its upstream transcriptional regulators, and the Argonaute-based evidence that separates direct target repression from correlative association. Across these tissues, miR-29a modulates oxidative metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and mitochondrial adaptation, largely through the PPARδ/PGC-1α axis, exerting complex and sometimes opposing effects depending on the tissue environment. We further examine miR-29a as a mediator of interorgan communication through extracellular vesicles, its responsiveness to exercise, and its emerging value as a biomarker and therapeutic target, while highlighting unresolved contradictions and translational hurdles. Because miR-29 family members act as tumor suppressors in most epithelial tissues, we also address the oncogenic risk inherent in nucleic acid strategies that lower miR-29a levels. Collectively, this mini-review positions miR-29a as a physiology-oriented integrator of metabolic remodeling and tissue-specific adaptation in metabolic disease.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism

title: AAOS Clinical Practice Guidelines for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Synopsis and Practice Implications.
abstract:
DESCRIPTION: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common peripheral nerve compression frequently encountered in primary care and internal medicine settings. The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (AAOS) developed updated evidence-based clinical practice guidelines in 2024 to improve outcomes and optimize diagnosis and management. This synopsis highlights recommendations most relevant to nonoperative clinicians, with an emphasis on efficient diagnosis, management, and appropriate referral.
METHODS: The AAOS guideline was developed by a multidisciplinary panel using a systematic review of the available literature. Guideline development involved reviewing the evidence, formulating recommendations, and grading them based on the strength of evidence and consensus, in line with established standards for trustworthy clinical practice guidelines.
RECOMMENDATIONS: The guidelines emphasize that carpal tunnel syndrome is a clinical diagnosis based on characteristic symptoms and examination findings. Strong evidence supports the use of validated clinical tools, such as the Carpal Tunnel Syndrome-6 (CTS-6), in patients with typical presentations, without routine reliance on ultrasonography or electrodiagnostic testing, which may be reserved for diagnostic uncertainty or potentially recurrent cases. Nonoperative therapies may provide short-term symptom relief; for example, corticosteroid injection demonstrates short-term benefit but does not alter the long-term disease course. Many commonly used interventions, including therapeutic ultrasound, oral corticosteroids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and platelet-rich plasma injections, lack evidence of clinical benefit and thus are not recommended. Surgical carpal tunnel release, when pursued for moderate to severe symptoms, thenar atrophy, or failure of nonoperative management, may be performed via open or endoscopic release. The guidelines recommend against routine pre-operative testing in otherwise healthy patients. These recommendations support efficient diagnosis, appropriate management, and timely referral while reducing unnecessary testing and low-value care.
authors: ASSH Quality and Value Care Committee

title: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate attenuates PAR-2-mediated inflammatory signaling and preserves markers of mitochondrial integrity in osteoarthritic chondrocytes.
abstract: Epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), the principal catechin of green tea, exhibits broad anti-inflammatory properties; however, its effect on protease-activated receptor-2 (PAR-2)-mediated signaling in osteoarthritis (OA) has not been investigated. Here, we report that EGCG (5-10 µM) dose-dependently suppresses PAR-2 expression at both mRNA and protein levels in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated human chondrocytes derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. This upstream inhibition attenuated ERK1/2 phosphorylation (pERK/total ERK ratio reduced below basal levels at 10 µM) and produced concordant suppression of three functionally linked effector arms: (i) pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, MCP-1), with near-maximal inhibition at 10 µM and a saturation plateau at 20 µM; (ii) the SOX4-ADAMTS-5 catabolic axis (81.9% and 66.2% protein reduction, respectively); and (iii) RANK/RANKL surface expression. EGCG also restored mitochondrial membrane potential and biomass to near-homeostatic levels. Crucially, small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated PAR-2 silencing reduced LPS-induced TNF-α by ~38% and substantially blunted EGCG's incremental efficacy, supporting PAR-2 as a predominant, though not exclusive, mediator of EGCG's anti-inflammatory action. The effective concentrations employed are physiologically attainable through dietary green tea consumption, as documented by a comprehensive survey of EGCG content across 36 commercial varieties. These findings support PAR-2 as a candidate upstream target of EGCG in OA chondrocytes and suggest a mechanistic model involving PAR-2 → ERK1/2 → TNF-α/SOX4/ADAMTS-5, through which a dietary polyphenol exerts coordinated anti-inflammatory and anti-catabolic effects, while preserving structural and thermodynamic markers of mitochondrial integrity.

title: Intensity-dependent microcurrent stimulation enhances BMSC-derived cartilage microtissue formation under defined culture conditions.
abstract: Engineering phenotypically favorable cartilage-like tissue from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) remains challenging because chondrogenic differentiation can be accompanied by insufficient cartilage-associated extracellular matrix accumulation and unfavorable hypertrophic and catabolic responses. Here, we established a microcurrent-assisted culture system for scaffold-free BMSC-derived cartilage microtissues (CMTs) and investigated the intensity-dependent effects of continuous unidirectional direct-current stimulation at 0, 50, 100, 150, 250, or 500 μA under a defined electrical and culture configuration. Among the tested conditions, 150 μA (nominal electrode current density, 3 μA/mm2) showed the most consistently favorable overall response, with enhanced cartilage-associated gene and protein expression, greater type II collagen- and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix accumulation, improved CMT morphology, and higher apparent mechanical properties. In contrast, 250 and 500 μA were associated with reduced cartilage-associated matrix formation and increased fibrotic, hypertrophic, catabolic, inflammatory, and apoptosis-related markers. The 150 μA condition was also associated with a distinct intracellular Ca2+ response pattern and increased NFATc1 nuclear localization; verapamil, BAPTA-AM, and cyclosporin A attenuated NFATc1 nuclear localization, supporting involvement of Ca2+/calcineurin/NFAT-related signaling without establishing a unique causal mechanism. After 2 weeks of xenogeneic subcutaneous implantation in nude mice, CMTs preconditioned at 150 μA exhibited greater cartilage-like matrix accumulation and higher apparent compressive properties than those preconditioned at 0 or 500 μA. These findings identify 150 μA as the best-performing tested condition under the present electrical configuration and provide short-term ectopic proof-of-concept evidence, while longer-term orthotopic studies are required to evaluate phenotypic stability, tissue integration, and functional outcomes in cartilage-defect models.

title: Conceptual Frameworks and Assessment of Readiness to Train in Endurance Exercise: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Readiness to train has emerged as a construct to guide daily training prescription and recovery management in endurance athletes. However, its conceptual basis, assessment, and methodological quality and validity remain inconsistently defined. This systematic review aimed to (1) identify how readiness is defined in endurance exercise and (2) categorize tools used to assess it. As a secondary aim, the review evaluated the methodological approach of the studies employing these tools.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were explored. Eligible studies included endurance athletes aged 18-65 years, evaluating readiness before or after training or competition. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed quality using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Fourteen studies were included.
RESULTS: Readiness definitions were inconsistent and frequently overlapped with related constructs such as recovery and fatigue. Ten studies used self-reported tools (fatigue, sleep, stress, and soreness). Nine studies assessed objective tools, including heart rate (HR) variability, resting HR, countermovement jump, and submaximal tests. HR variability-based approaches and individualized feedback were used to track autonomic recovery and guide training prescription, while on-field indices (eg, HR-running speed, HR-running power, countermovement jump) provided neuromuscular insights, although they can also be influenced by cardiovascular and metabolic factors. Overall, there was considerable heterogeneity in tools and their combinations, highlighting the lack of standardized approaches to assess readiness to train. Seven studies combined subjective and objective measures, suggesting a more comprehensive monitoring strategy. However, many of these tools were primarily used to assess related constructs (eg, fatigue, recovery, and training adaptation) rather than directly predict performance; consequently, their ability to predict performance outcomes remained limited or was not even assessed.
CONCLUSION: This review highlights substantial conceptual ambiguity, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity in readiness assessment. A multidimensional framework conceptualizing readiness as a dynamic psychophysiological state influenced by stress, recovery, and contextual factors may support more structured and meaningful monitoring in endurance athletes.

title: Breast Injuries in Women's Rugby Union: A Comparison of Prospective and Retrospective Surveillance.
abstract: Retrospective research has reported a high prevalence of breast injuries in women's rugby union (RU); however, most injuries are not reported to medical staff. This study compared the incidence and severity of breast injuries collected both prospectively and retrospectively over a comparable match exposure period. Prospective surveillance was conducted by clinicians (n = 14) using an online injury surveillance system across 140 RU players. Retrospective surveillance was conducted using an anonymous online survey completed by 370 RU players. Injury incidence was calculated per 1000 hours of match exposure. Severity was assessed using breast pain, bruising and swelling, ability to continue play, perceived effect on performance, and long-term breast changes. Three breast injuries were prospectively recorded over 1204 hours of competition (2.5 injuries/1000 hours). In contrast, 144 breast injuries were reported retrospectively over 5055 hours of competition (28.5 injuries/1000 hours). The retrospective injury rate was significantly higher than the prospective rate (IRR = 11.4, 95% CI: 3.15-41.73; p < 0.002). Ninety-six percent (n = 139) of retrospectively reported injuries had not been disclosed to medical staff. Injury severity was similar between surveillance methods, with bruising commonly reported, all players continuing to participate despite injury, and over half perceiving a negative effect on performance. Long-term breast changes were reported by 6% (n = 8) of players. The substantially lower incidence recorded prospectively suggests that breast injuries are underreported in women's RU. Improved reporting and surveillance strategies are required to better capture breast injuries and support female athlete health and performance.

title: Long-Term Failure Rate of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using All-Inside 4-Stranded Semitendinosus Autograft Is 20.5.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate outcomes (graft failure, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures, and knee stability) after primary isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction using the all-inside technique with 4-stranded semitendinosus autograft fixed between 2 adjustable-loop cortical suspension devices, with a minimum follow-up of 10 years.
METHODS: Patients who underwent primary isolated ACL reconstruction using the all-inside 4-stranded semitendinosus between January 2011 and January 2013, with a minimum of 10-year follow-up, were included. Patients completed a standardized questionnaire and were offered a follow-up consultation. The questionnaire included the Tegner, ACL-Return to Sport after Injury, Subjective Knee Value, subjective International Knee Documentation Committee, and assessment of graft failure. Clinical evaluations and laxity measurements were conducted during follow-up consultations.
RESULTS: At a mean follow-up of 138 months (range: 122-159), 156 patients completed the questionnaire, and 111 were clinically evaluated. The mean age was 39.6 ± 9.7 years (range: 15-62). Graft failure occurred in 20.5% of cases (32/156). The mean decrease in Tegner was 1.03 ± 1.23 points, and 51% returned to their preinjury sport level. The median preoperative Tegner was 7.0 (interquartile range: 6.0-7.0). A higher preoperative Tegner was associated with an increased risk of graft failure (P = .016). Graft failure occurred in 23% of males and 16.6% of females (P = .461). Patients with grafts sized ≤8 mm (n = 85) had a failure rate of 17.5%, compared with 23.9% for grafts >8 mm (P = .441). The mean subjective International Knee Documentation Committee was 85.6 ± 13.5, Subjective Knee Value 79.2 ± 22.1, and ACL-Return to Sport after Injury 69.5 ± 26.5. Among patients without reported graft failure, 16.5% exhibited >3 mm differential anterior laxity, and 28% had a pivot-shift score ≥2.
CONCLUSIONS: At a minimum 10-year follow-up, primary isolated ACL reconstruction using an all-inside 4-stranded semitendinosus autograft showed a 20.5% graft failure rate, despite favorable patient-reported outcomes. A higher preoperative Tegner showed a trend toward increased graft failure.

title: Five-Year Outcomes and Return to Sport After Arthroscopic Bankart Repair in Young Patients With Minimal (<10%) or No Glenoid Bone Loss.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arthroscopic Bankart repair is commonly used to address anterior instability in adolescents and young adults with no or minimal bone loss. However, failure rates remain high, particularly in high-risk populations.
PURPOSE/HYPOTHESIS: The purpose of this study was to evaluate clinical outcomes, return-to-sport (RTS) rates, and predictors of failure after arthroscopic Bankart repair in patients ≤24 years of age with minimal glenoid bone loss. It was hypothesized that patients would demonstrate favorable outcomes, low recurrence rates, and high RTS rates, and smaller distance-to-dislocation (DTD) measurements, and contact sports participation would be associated with failure.
STUDY DESIGN: Case series; Level of evidence, 4.
METHODS: The data of patients with anterior shoulder instability and minimal bone loss (<10%) who underwent primary arthroscopic Bankart repair between 2006 and 2020 were retrospectively analyzed. Remplissage was not performed. Data collected included preoperative instability events, patient-reported outcome measures, satisfaction, radiographic measurements (glenoid bone loss, glenoid track, and DTD), and RTS outcomes. Failure was defined as re-dislocation or recurrent instability requiring surgery.
RESULTS: A total of 130 patients were evaluated; 18 were excluded, leaving 112. Of these, 96 patients (85.7%) were available for the final follow-up (mean age, 19.9 ± 3.1 years; mean follow-up, 68.4 ± 42.7 months). All clinical outcomes improved significantly (P < .05) except for the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey Mental Component Summary score. The median satisfaction score was 9 (IQR, 8-10). Participation in contact sports was associated with failure, while other risk factors were not. RTS was achieved by 96.1% of patients; however, only 57.1% returned to their preinjury level. Fewer preoperative dislocation events were associated with successful return to full activity (P = .04). The recurrence rate was 33.3%, and revision surgery was required in 19 patients (19.8%).
CONCLUSION: Arthroscopic Bankart repair was associated with high rates of recurrence and revision surgery in a series of patients ≤24 years of age without glenoid bone loss. In those who did not require revision surgery, clinical outcomes and RTS rates were high. Contact sports participation was associated with failure. A greater number of preoperative instability events negatively influence RTS outcomes. Arthroscopic Bankart repair in this population is safe and has a low complication rate, but the failure rate remains considerable.

title: Weightbearing CT in the Evaluation of Athletic Foot and Ankle Injuries.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Subtle foot and ankle injuries in athletes, including syndesmotic sprains, ligamentous Lisfranc injuries, osteochondral lesions of the talus, and proximal fifth metatarsal stress fractures, may be underestimated or misclassified on conventional imaging. This review summarizes the current role of weightbearing CT (WBCT) in their evaluation, focusing on quantitative parameters, recent technical advances, and their potential influence on clinical decision-making.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence has shifted WBCT from qualitative assessment toward reproducible three-dimensional quantification. Volumetric assessment and distance mapping improve characterization of syndesmotic instability, while external-rotation stress can reveal abnormalities not evident during neutral standing. In the midfoot, triplanar realignment and side-to-side comparison improve the reliability of Lisfranc measurements and support detection of subtle instability. Distance mapping permits reproducible quantification of osteochondral lesion surface area, depth, and volume and may improve consistency in surgical planning. WBCT has also characterized sport-specific alignment patterns and a morphologic and bone-density phenotype associated with proximal fifth metatarsal stress fractures. Semiautomated segmentation and deep-learning methods may further reduce observer dependence and analysis time. WBCT provides three-dimensional measurements under physiologic load that complement clinical examination and conventional imaging in selected athletic foot and ankle conditions. Its greatest current value lies in characterizing subtle instability, malalignment, and osseous morphology when these findings may alter treatment planning. However, most available evidence is retrospective and derived from symptomatic or injured cohorts. Prospective studies are needed to validate diagnostic thresholds, determine whether WBCT-derived parameters predict injury or outcomes, and define their role in routine athletic screening and return-to-sport decision-making.

title: The Role of Physical Preparation in Motorsport Athletes Across Different Vehicle Types: A Narrative Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite motorsport's widespread appeal, early performance models did not consider drivers as athletes, and even drivers often struggled with this classification, which historically contributed to their exclusion from research focused on athletic performance. Slowly but steadily, this paradigm has been changing.
PURPOSE: To review the evolution of physical conditioning in land-based motorsports and to examine the specific physiological and physical demands imposed on drivers by different vehicle types. A narrative review was conducted to synthesize historical perspectives, physiological demands, and training approaches in motorsport. Peer-reviewed studies, practical reports, opinion articles, and relevant online materials were analyzed to describe the evolution of the physical conditioning required across racing categories. The physical demands in motorsports are characterized by sustained cardiovascular strain, significant neuromuscular loading, large and sustained G-force exposure, and pronounced thermal stress. These demands vary according to vehicle type. Closed-wheel drivers are particularly exposed to prolonged heat stress and require comprehensive muscular endurance and thermoregulatory adaptation. Open-wheel drivers experience large G-forces, demanding exceptional neck and lower-limb strength. Two-wheel riders require enhanced handgrip strength, dynamic neuromuscular control, and high levels of aerobic capacity.
CONCLUSIONS: Tailored conditioning programs addressing the distinct physiological, neuromuscular, and thermoregulatory demands of each motorsport category are closely linked to performance and safety. Further systematic evaluation of the empirical evidence is necessary to enhance the ecological validity of training recommendations and strengthen their application in competitive motorsport.

title: Acute and Chronic Effects of Parachute-Resisted Sprint Training on Sprint Performance and Sprint Mechanics: A Systematic Review with GRADE Assessment.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parachute-resisted sprint training (PRST) is a practical field-based resisted-sprint method that uses aerodynamic drag to provide sprint-specific overload. Although PRST has been widely used in athletic settings, evidence on its acute mechanical effects and chronic training adaptations remains heterogeneous.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aimed to synthesize the acute and chronic effects of PRST on sprint performance, sprint mechanics, neuromuscular responses, and sprint-related physiological outcomes in healthy, physically active, and athletic populations.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus on 17th May 2026. Original empirical studies were eligible if they examined PRST or parachute-resisted sprinting and reported outcomes related to sprint performance, biomechanics, neuromuscular responses, or sprint-related physiology. Studies were synthesized narratively and grouped into acute and chronic evidence streams. Methodological quality was assessed using the Modified Downs and Black checklist, and certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included (8 acute and 9 chronic). In acute comparisons, PRST consistently reduced sprint velocity or increased sprint time; where directly reported, velocity reductions were approximately 3.4-6% relative to unresisted sprinting. Larger parachute conditions generally produced greater velocity decrements and changes in horizontal force or impulse variables. Chronic studies reported improvements in selected sprint outcomes, including 0-10 m, 10-20 m, and 0-20 m splits in one randomized study; other studies reported improvements such as 3.48% in 60-yd performance and 0.618 s in 100-m performance. However, chronic studies' findings were heterogeneous, and evidence for maximal velocity, neuromuscular or energetic outcomes, and population-specific effects remained limited.
CONCLUSIONS: PRST appears to provide a practical, sprint-specific overload and may improve selected sprint performance outcomes. However, the current evidence base is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous protocols, poor quantification of resistance, inconsistent reporting of outcomes, and limited comparator control. Based on GRADE, confidence in the evidence is generally 'low' to 'very low' across most outcomes. Trial Registration (OSF) https://osf.io/56nct DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/8SJW4.

title: Objective Return-to-Sport (RTS) Decision Frameworks for Adolescent Shoulder and Elbow Injuries: Tests, Thresholds and Exercise Targets.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent shoulder and elbow injuries are increasing due to sports specialization and year-round training, yet return-to-sport decisions typically rely on adult-derived heuristics that fail to address the unique physiology, growth plate vulnerability, and recovery needs of developing athletes aged 10-19 years.
OBJECTIVE: This review proposes a novel, objective three-pillar RTS framework integrating: (1) foundational tissue capacity, (2) dynamic movement quality and neuromuscular control, and (3) sport-specific load tolerance. We synthesize current evidence to establish provisional, consensus-based adolescent thresholds and provide a practical bedside toolkit for immediate clinical implementation.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative synthesis of contemporary original evidence, consensus recommendations, and validation studies relevant to adolescent shoulder and elbow rehabilitation. Evidence was critically appraised for youth-specific validation, with explicit distinction between evidence-based interventions and emerging aspirational technologies requiring prospective adolescent cohort validation.
RESULTS: We propose a hybrid benchmarking model combining limb symmetry indices (LSI ≥90%) with population-referenced percentiles (≥25th percentile for age/sex/sport) as provisional, consensus-based thresholds. A three-stage progression is outlined: Clinic-ready (pain-free ROM, isometric IR/ER LSI ≥90%), Training-ready (dynamic rotational LSI ≥90%, preserved scapular kinematics), and Game-ready (sport-specific tolerance with 5% velocity loss during simulated exposure). We provide a low-resource bedside toolkit including belt-stabilized hand-held dynamometry, Closed Kinetic Chain Upper Extremity Stability Test (CKCUEST), Push-Up Plus, Athletic Shoulder positions, seated medicine-ball throw, and simple interval tolerance simulations with specific protocols and thresholds. A stepwise algorithm advances from capacity → movement quality → load tolerance with targeted remediation at each gate.
CONCLUSION: Moving beyond time-based or adult-derived heuristics, this objective multidimensional framework aligns tissue recovery with sport-specific demands through quantifiable metrics. While provisional thresholds require further adolescent validation, the framework offers an evidence-guided pathway that mitigates reinjury risk, restores performance, and supports safe reintegration into sport. Implementation requires adolescent-specific normative databases, stakeholder communication, and cost-effective technological integration for equitable adoption.

title: A Six-Day High-Intensity Interval Training Microcycle Improves Selected Indicators of Endurance Performance in Well-Trained Female Cross-Country Skiers and Biathletes.
abstract: We compared the effects of a 6-day high-intensity interval training (HIT) microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period (HITblock) with a time-matched period of continued regular training (REG) on endurance performance in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes. Seventeen athletes (maximal oxygen consumption ( V ˙ O 2 max ): 55.1 (5.2) mL·min-1 kg-1) were assigned to either HITblock or REG. No differences in training volume or intensity were observed between the groups during the 4 weeks preceding the intervention. During the intervention, HITblock completed five HIT sessions over 6 days (6 × 5-min work intervals; target rate of perceived exertion:17-18), with increased HIT replacing part of their habitual training and thereby reducing overall training load, whereas REG continued habitual training, including 3-4 moderate- or high-intensity interval sessions. Endurance performance was assessed during roller ski skating and included 15-min time-trial average velocity (velocity15-min), velocity at 4 mmol·L-1 blood lactate (velocity4mmol), and velocity during the final minute of incremental V ˙ O 2 max testing ( velocity V ˙ O 2 max ). HITblock demonstrated greater improvements than REG in velocity V ˙ O 2 max (3.6 (2.1)% versus 1.2 (1.6)%, p = 0.024) and velocity4mmol (4.4 (2.9)% versus 0.0 (4.4)%, p = 0.023), whereas changes in velocity15-min did not differ between groups (5.4 (5.0)% versus 1.3 (3.4)%, p = 0.083). An exploratory composite performance index combining these outcomes demonstrated superior improvements in HITblock compared with REG (4.5 (2.8)% versus 0.9 (2.6)%, p = 0.017). These findings indicate that a 6-day HIT microcycle followed by a 5-day active recovery period is associated with greater improvements in selected endurance performance indicators compared with continued regular training in well-trained female cross-country skiers and biathletes.

title: Effects and Moderators of High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) on Physiological Adaptations Among Team-Sport Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is widely used in team sports, but the influence of participant and programme characteristics on physiological adaptations remains unclear. Five databases (Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CNKI) were searched initially on 25 April 2025 and updated on 21 December 2025. Mixed-effects models were used to estimate Hedges' g and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Forty-six studies involving 1204 athletes were included. Compared with regular sport-specific training alone, HIIT produced positive effects on maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max; g = 0.76, 95% CI [0.61, 0.92]), maximal aerobic power (g = 0.43, 95% CI [0.04, 0.82]), ventilatory threshold (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.53, 0.88]), Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance (g = 1.02, 95% CI [0.76, 1.28]), and 30-s Wingate peak (g = 0.91, 95% CI [0.67, 1.16]) and mean power (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.39, 1.01]). Effects on body composition were generally unclear. Mutually adjusted multivariable meta-regression identified no convincing evidence of differences in VO2max or Yo-Yo intermittent recovery test performance effects by sex or training level. Longer training duration was associated with greater VO2max effects. In exploratory analyses, model predictions indicated increases in VO2max of 2.56 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI [1.54, 3.58]) after approximately 5 weeks and 5.11 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI [3.32, 6.91]) after approximately 10 weeks. Shorter between-repetition recovery was associated with greater VO2max effects, although other programme variables were estimated imprecisely. Overall, adding HIIT to regular sport-specific training improves aerobic and anaerobic performance in trained team-sport athletes, whereas effects on body composition are limited. Associations involving programme characteristics should be interpreted cautiously because they were derived from study-level meta-regression. Trial Registration: PROSPERO Registration CRD42024609379.

title: A rare traumatic triad: Open bicondylar non-conjoint Hoffa fracture with partial tibial tubercle and medial epicondyle avulsions - A case report and biomechanical analysis.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles are rare intra-articular injuries, and the simultaneous occurrence of a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture with a partial anterior tibial tubercle avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion constitutes an exceptionally complex traumatic triad. We report the case of a 35-year-old male motorcyclist who sustained this "floating" articular block injury (AO/OTA 33-B3.3) following a high-velocity accident. Diagnostic assessment utilizing Computed Tomography with 3D reconstruction revealed a vertical Letenneur Type II fracture of the medial condyle and a comminuted Letenneur Type I fracture of the lateral condyle, complicated by significant rotational instability. Surgical management prioritized the posterior femoral instability through a double posterior approach, which allowed for direct visualization and anatomical reduction. Fixation was achieved using posterior-to-anterior headless compression screws, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to neutralize shear forces, while the medial epicondyle was anatomically reduced and fixed; the stable partial tibial tubercle avulsion was treated conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated excellent functional recovery with 120 degrees of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a successful return to recreational sports. This case highlights the importance of the double posterior approach and "targeted rigidity" in managing multidirectional instability, permitting early mobilization even in the presence of complex extensor mechanism involvement.
INTRODUCTION: Coronal shear fractures of the distal femoral condyles (Hoffa fractures) are rare intra-articular injuries, with bicondylar patterns being exceptionally uncommon. A non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture combined with a partial anterior tibial tubercle (ATT) avulsion and a medial epicondyle avulsion represents a complex, "floating" articular block that challenges standard treatment algorithms. This case report analyzes the biomechanics and management of this rare traumatic triad.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old male motorcyclist presented with a Gustilo-Anderson Type I open knee injury following a high-velocity crash involving hyper-flexion and valgus stress. CT imaging confirmed a non-conjoint bicondylar Hoffa fracture (AO/OTA 33-B3.3, Bagaria Type 3). The lateral condyle presented as a Letenneur Type I fracture with extensive comminution, while the medial condyle was a Letenneur Type II vertical fracture. Associated injuries included an Ogden Type I partial ATT avulsion and a Watson-Jones Type I medial epicondyle avulsion.Surgical management utilized a double posterior approach to visualize and reduce the posterior fragments. Fixation involved headless cannulated compression screws for both condyles, augmented by a posterior buttress plate on the lateral column to resist shear forces. The medial epicondyle was refixed with a screw and washer, while the stable ATT avulsion was managed conservatively. At the two-year follow-up, the patient achieved excellent functional outcomes, including 120° of flexion, a Lysholm score of 91, and a Tegner Activity Scale score of 7.
CONCLUSION: Managing this complex triad requires a thorough understanding of the injury mechanism, which involves coronal shear, valgus stress, and eccentric extensor loading. 3D CT reconstruction is mandatory for planning, and a double posterior approach provides superior visualization for anatomical reduction and posterior-to-anterior fixation. Rigid fixation, particularly using anti-glide plating for the lateral column, permits early mobilization and the conservative management of stable associated injuries, leading to high patient satisfaction.

title: Dose-dependent effects of sodium bicarbonate supplementation combined with sprint interval training on performance adaptations in basketball players: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sprint interval training (SIT) effectively improves physical performance in team-sport athletes, while sodium bicarbonate (Sb) supplementation may enhance training adaptations. However, the dose-dependent effects of Sb during SIT remain unclear in basketball players. Therefore, this study examined the effects of two Sb doses combined with SIT on physical performance adaptations in basketball players.
METHODS: Forty trained male basketball players (age: 21.6 ± 2.0 years, height: 185.4 ± 3.5 cm, body mass: 84.1 ± 4.4 kg) were recruited and randomly assigned to four groups: SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + placebo (PL) (n = 10), and control (CON) (n = 10). The intervention lasted four weeks during the preparatory phase of the season. Participants in the training groups performed SIT three times per week in addition to their regular basketball training. The SIT protocol consisted of four sets of ten 5-second maximal sprints, with 20 seconds of active recovery between repetitions and 2 minutes of rest between sets. All 40 enrolled participants successfully completed the 4-week intervention, resulting in a 0% dropout rate. Performance assessments conducted before and after the intervention included countermovement vertical jump (CMVJ), standing long jump (SLJ), 20 m sprint, Illinois change-of-direction speed (CODS), Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (Yo-Yo IR1), and Wingate anaerobic power (peak power output [PPO] and mean power output [MPO]).
RESULTS: All training groups showed significant improvements in physical performance variables over time (p < 0.05). Significant group by time interaction effects were observed for all performance variables (p ≤ 0.001), indicating that the SIT groups showed more gains compared with the CON group. Both Sb supplementation groups demonstrated greater improvements than the SIT + PL group in CMVJ, SLJ, sprint performance, CODS, Yo-Yo IR1 distance, PPO, and MPO (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb group exhibited significantly greater performance enhancements than the SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb group across all measured variables.
CONCLUSION: Four weeks of SIT improved performance in trained basketball players, with Sb supplementation providing additional dose-dependent benefits (0.45 > 0.3 g⋅kg-1). While the higher dose yielded superior adaptations, its practical application should be balanced against potential gastrointestinal discomfort and individual tolerance to ensure long-term athlete compliance.

title: Nitric oxide precursor interventions for post-exercise delayed onset muscle soreness: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) commonly follows high-intensity or unaccustomed exercise. Nitric oxide (NO) precursors may reduce DOMS, but their effects remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate NO precursor interventions across recovery time points.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched to February 2026 for randomized controlled trials in healthy adults. Interventions were classified into four nodes: beetroot-derived nitrate, watermelon-derived citrulline, synthetic or isolated amino acid precursors (L-arginine and citrulline malate), and watermelon plus added citrulline. Random-effects network meta-analyses were conducted separately at 24, 48, and 72 h. Effects were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); SUCRA rankings were exploratory. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using RoB 2 and CINeMA, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses examining robustness.
RESULTS: Nineteen trials involving 356 participants were included. At 24 h, watermelon plus added citrulline (SMD = -0.97, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.31) and beetroot-derived nitrate (SMD = -0.67, 95% CI -1.14 to -0.20) significantly reduced DOMS vs. placebo. At 48 h, beetroot-derived nitrate was the only intervention with a significant benefit (SMD = -1.18, 95% CI -1.91 to -0.45). No active intervention differed significantly from placebo at 72 h, while evidence for differences between active interventions was limited, with only watermelon plus added citrulline showing a significant advantage over synthetic or isolated amino acid precursors at 24 h. Beetroot-derived nitrate significantly reduced DOMS vs. placebo in the trained subgroup but not in the untrained subgroup. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the findings, although the beetroot-derived nitrate estimate was sensitive to some restrictions related to the exercise-induced muscle damage model.
CONCLUSION: NO precursor supplementation may reduce post-exercise DOMS at specific recovery time points, particularly with beetroot-derived nitrate and watermelon plus added citrulline. However, evidence for differences between active interventions remains limited, and the sparse network, substantial heterogeneity, and low certainty of evidence preclude firm clinical conclusions.
